thread:
maya: Heads-up deferred-chop plan sketch landed in the repo. High level: we propose splitting Enricher into a thin demux (per-tenant routing, ownership tags) + stateful worker pool. Goal: reduce lateral tenant blast radius and make hot-prefix caching per-tenant. Looking for rollout/rollback criteria thoughts.
sanjay: important direction, +1. Questions: how do we handle prefix ownership transfers during rollouts? that was painful last time.
maya: good call. Plan is to use a transfer window: owner pod marks prefix stale and writes owner_version; new owner warms before accepting writes. We'll add a CS-style two-phase swap and a small ownership grace TTL (30s).
owen: need to be careful with KV repop churn; if we shift too many prefixes at once we'll thrash caches. We should gate by prefix-rank. Only move top-k per tenant each wave.
lucy: operationally we need explicit rollback triggers. Suggest autopause if per-tenant cache-hit drops >10% and p95 >1.25x baseline for 15m. Also record a migration-plan artifact in S3 per rollout with owned-prefix list.
kevin: from infra side: we can reserve a 10% GPU headroom for waves and enable affinity for dedicated pools to avoid noisy neighbour. Also add a metric for cross-pod lookup-rate (xpl_count) so we can see fanout increase.
sanjay: agree. Also add a invariant check in the deploy pipeline: after the wave we must ensure at-least-one owner per prefix and no prefix in limbo >TTL.
maya: ok I'll codify that. Also adding a prewarm job that runs prior to cutover: seed caches for top-100 prefixes per tenant; job runs in parallel but rate-limited to avoid saturating GPU.
owen: implement feature-flag gating: rollout.wavesize, rollout.topk, rollout.prewarm=true/false, rollout.affinity=true/false. Keep default conservative.
lucy: doc action: I'll draft the runbook section covering the transfer window, rollback thresholds, and how to inspect xpl_count heatmap.
infra-bot: alert rule created: enricher.ownership.migration.cache-drop (>10%) (id em-4421)
maya: one more tradeoff: this approach increases control-plane complexity (owner_version bookkeeping). Tech debt paydown suggestion: after stable cutovers, we should converge owner_version into the prefix metadata store and retire the adapter shim in 3 months.
sanjay: make that a tracked ticket in the platform backlog and assign an engineer for the follow-up refactor.
maya: will do. Timeline: planning spike next week, small canary (single tenant) in two weeks if spike is green. I'll update the PR with gating knobs and the prewarm job config.
lucy: cool. ping me when the canary is green and I'll run the rollback drill with SRE.
maya: thanks all. Very keen to reduce cross-tenant impacts but want safe, observable migration path.
